meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.
Starting a question: а жвачку?. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Habitually or in general. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to take', paired with 'взять'.
'брать' alone often means this, in talk about officials

examples.trans: We have to take all the money.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: predicative: очень вкусно = it's delicious
Вкусно готовить = to cook well. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('tasty, delicious').

examples.trans: The bread rings are very tasty.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, присядьте. Попробуйте чай с сушками, очень вкусные.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, have a seat. Try the tea with bread rings, they're very tasty.

meanings.note: Pointing at something. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.
Emphasis. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'salary' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Двадцать тысяч я вычту из вашей зарплаты!
examples.trans: I will deduct twenty thousand from your salary!
I will deduct it from your pension.

meanings.note: Location; for direction use 'куда'. Core Russian adv meaning 'where' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Где-то здесь была, а теперь нет.
examples.trans: It used to be somewhere here, and now it's gone.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'moron, idiot (colloq.)' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новый дебил.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new moron.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'dessert' (from 'desservir', to clear the table).

examples.text: Гости в зале уже спрашивают новые десерты.
examples.trans: Guests in the dining room are already asking for new desserts.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.
Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Core Russian adv meaning 'more; still; yet' in everyday speech.
Ещё больше = even more. Core Russian adv meaning 'more; still; yet' in everyday speech.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Location. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.
emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
+ genitive. Core Russian part meaning 'no; there isn't' in everyday speech.
usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
For masculine and neuter things. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.
Locative / directional adverb.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'pair, couple, match' in everyday Russian.

meanings.en: match (in a relationship: я не пара вам = I'm no match for you)
meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'pair, couple, match' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я понимаю, я не пара вам.
examples.trans: I understand I'm no match for you.
They are a very handsome couple.

examples.text: Я понимаю, я не пара вам. Вы красавец, а я старая.
examples.trans: I understand I'm no match for you. You're a handsome man, and I'm old.

meanings.note: Informal. Common masculine noun meaning 'guy, lad; boyfriend' in everyday Russian.
Мой парень = my boyfriend. Common masculine noun meaning 'guy, lad; boyfriend' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Всегда мечтала познакомиться с друзьями моего парня.
examples.trans: I've always dreamed of meeting my boyfriend's friends.

meanings.note: Monthly retirement payment. Common feminine noun meaning 'pension; retirement' in everyday Russian.
На пенсии = retired. Common feminine noun meaning 'pension; retirement' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Grandma has been retired for a long time.

examples.text: А тебе этого мало? У меня пенсия двенадцать тысяч!
examples.trans: And is that a small sum to you? My pension is twelve thousand!

meanings.note: substantivized neuter adjective, declines like an adjective

examples.text: Мы купили свежие пирожные к чаю.
examples.trans: We bought fresh pastries for tea.

examples.text: Я пирожные принёс! Может, мы пока чаю попьём?
examples.trans: I brought pastries! Maybe we could have some tea in the meantime?

meanings.note: платить за + accusative = to pay for

examples.text: А вашу работу вернуть можно. И мы хорошо платим.
examples.trans: But we can get your job back for you. And we pay well.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чувствовать'). Used in Russian as a perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to feel'.

examples.trans: The guest smelled the pleasant aroma of the dish.

examples.text: Инспектор точно почувствует вкус крепкого алкоголя.
examples.trans: The inspector will definitely taste strong alcohol.

examples.text: Поверь мне, никто не почувствует разницу!
examples.trans: Believe me, nobody will feel the difference!

meanings.note: Literally 'until the meeting'. Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'meeting; date' in everyday Russian.
Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'meeting; date' in everyday Russian.
Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'devour, gobble up'.

examples.text: Кто опять успел сожрать все свежие круассаны до открытия?
examples.trans: Who managed to devour all the fresh croissants before opening again?

examples.text: Голодный пёс за секунду сожрал целый кусок дорогой вырезки.
examples.trans: In a second the hungry dog gobbled up a whole piece of expensive tenderloin.

meanings.note: A whole portion; completed action. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to eat (up)', paired with 'есть'.

examples.text: Скоро. А пока я есть хочу, слона бы съел!
examples.trans: Soon. But for now I'm hungry, I could eat an elephant!

meanings.note: + genitive or infinitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to demand', paired with 'потребовать'.

examples.trans: We demand that house arrest be replaced.
What are you demanding from me?

examples.text: Мы требуем заменить домашний арест. Нужна подписка о невыезде.
examples.trans: We demand that house arrest be replaced. What's needed is a travel ban.

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'owner', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: The restaurant owner personally greets the guests.
The owner is busy in the kitchen for now.

examples.text: Вовсе нет, я жду хозяина ресторана.
examples.trans: Not at all, I am waiting for the restaurant owner.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.
